title: Induction on qcqs algebraic spaces by elementary distinguished squares
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $X$ a quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Quasi-compactness means that every open cover has a finite subcover, and quasi-separatedness means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact on scheme tests. An elementary distinguished square $(U\subset W,p:V\to W)$ means an open immersion $U\to W$ (identifying $U$ with an open subspace [def-a1-space-open-subspace]), a representable etale map $p$, and an isomorphism $V\times_WZ\to Z$, where $Z$ is the reduced closed subspace with underlying set $|W|\setminus|U|$ [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support], the point sets carrying the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Its fourth vertex is $U\times_WV$. Let $P$ be an isomorphism-invariant property of etale maps $T\to X$ with $T$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated; $T$ may be an algebraic space. Assume (a) $P(T)$ holds for every affine scheme $T$ etale over $X$; and (b) for every elementary distinguished square $(U\subset W,V\to W)$ over $X$ with $W$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, $U$ quasi-compact, and $V$ affine, if $P(U)$, $P(V)$, and $P(U\times_WV)$ hold, then $P(W)$ holds. All objects mentioned in (b) belong to the domain of $P$. Then $P(T)$ holds for every quasi-compact and quasi-separated algebraic space etale over $X$, including $T=X$. The empty affine scheme is allowed.

source.place: Tag 08GP (lemma-induction-principle); elementary distinguished squares as used in this lemma and in Tag 08JK (lemma-unbounded-relative-mayer-vietoris).

proof.text: Fix any qcqs etale object $T\to X$. Every quasi-compact open $A\subset T$ is quasi-separated: its absolute diagonal is the pullback of the diagonal of $T$ along $A\times A\to T\times T$, and quasi-compactness is preserved by base change [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Thus these opens are in the domain of $P$. Open inclusions and their composites with etale maps are etale on scheme tests. For a quasi-compact open $A\subset T$ and an affine scheme $B\to T$, the inclusion $A\to T$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence]; its base change $A\times_TB\to B$ is quasi-compact by [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]. Consequently $A\times_TB$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of $B$, hence quasi-separated by the same diagonal argument. These checks will apply to all overlaps below.

source.place: Tag 08GP (lemma-induction-principle), domain and quasi-compactness checks in both proof paragraphs

proof.text: First suppose $T$ is a scheme. Apply [lem-sc-invert-s-cohomology-induction] to the property $Q(A)=P(A\to T\to X)$ of quasi-compact opens of $T$. For an affine open, (a) gives $Q$. For $A$ quasi-compact open and $B$ affine open, $(A\subset A\cup B,B\to A\cup B)$ is an elementary distinguished square: the reduced complement of $A$ lies in $B$, so its inverse image in $B$ is itself. The overlap is $A\cap B$, and step 1 verifies the required domain conditions. Hypothesis (b) supplies exactly the union implication of the cited scheme-induction lemma. It follows that $P(T)$ holds for every qcqs scheme etale over $X$, and also for all its quasi-compact open subschemes.

source.place: Tag 08GP (lemma-induction-principle), first proof paragraph; coherent.tex Tag 08DR (lemma-induction-principle)

proof.text: For general $T$, pass to the algebraic space $j_!T$ over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ of [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers]: by its parts (2) and (3), open subspaces, etale scheme charts, fibre products and reduced closed subspaces of $T$ and of $j_!T$ correspond, and quasi-compactness and the absolute diagonal are unchanged. Apply [lem-sfb-qcqs-space-splitting-filtration] to $j_!T$ and transport the result back to $T$. Obtain quasi-compact opens $\emptyset=U_{n+1}\subset U_n\subset\cdots\subset U_1=T$ and surjective etale maps $f_p:V_p\to U_p$ with $V_p$ quasi-compact separated schemes, isomorphic over the reduced complements $Z_p=U_p\setminus U_{p+1}$. Each open and each chart inherits its map to $S$ from $T$, so this use of the absolute filtration imposes no condition on the original base $S$. The induction assertion is $P(U_p)$, descending from $p=n+1$ to $1$. Its initial case holds by (a), since the empty scheme is affine. Assume $P(U_{p+1})$. Choose a finite affine open cover $V_p=\bigcup_{i=1}^mV_{p,i}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover].

source.place: Tag 08GP (lemma-induction-principle), second proof paragraph through the finite affine covering; decent-spaces.tex Tag 07ST (lemma-filter-quasi-compact-quasi-separated); spaces.tex Tags 03I4, 04SG (change of base scheme)

proof.text: Set $W_0=U_{p+1}$ and $W_i=U_{p+1}\cup\bigcup_{j\le i}f_p(V_{p,j})$. By [lem-a1-space-etale-open-image] the images are open subspaces and quasi-compact; finite unions are quasi-compact by taking finite subcovers on each member. Step 1 makes each $W_i$ quasi-separated. Surjectivity gives $W_m=U_p$. Since $f_p(V_{p,i})\subset W_i$, the open-image clause factors $V_{p,i}\to V_p\to U_p$ through $W_i$, and the factor is representable etale, its scheme base changes being those over $U_p$. The pairs $(W_{i-1}\subset W_i,V_{p,i}\to W_i)$ are elementary distinguished squares, as follows directly. Let $C_i$ be the reduced closed complement of $W_{i-1}$ in $W_i$. Its support lies in $Z_p\cap W_i$, so $C_i$ factors through this reduced closed subspace: on affine charts, a function vanishing at every point of the reduced source is zero. The inverse image of $Z_p\cap W_i$ under $f_p$ is that same space. Under this isomorphism the inverse image of $C_i$ lies entirely in $V_{p,i}$: every point of $W_i\setminus W_{i-1}$ is in the image of $V_{p,i}$ by the definition of $W_i$. The open subspace in question is therefore the whole inverse image, by [lem-a1-space-point-open-calculus]. Thus $V_{p,i}\times_{W_i}C_i\to C_i$ is an isomorphism. The reduced subspaces used here exist uniquely by [lem-sfb-space-reduced-closed-support]; restricting one to an open remains reduced and has the prescribed support.

source.place: Tag 08GP (lemma-induction-principle), construction of W_{p,i}; Tag 08GN (lemma-make-more-elementary-distinguished-squares), restriction argument written out

proof.text: For each $i$, (a) gives $P(V_{p,i})$. The overlap $W_{i-1}\times_{W_i}V_{p,i}$ is a quasi-compact open subscheme of the affine $V_{p,i}$ by the checks in step 1; it is therefore a qcqs scheme etale over $X$. Step 2 gives $P$ for this overlap. Starting with $P(W_0)=P(U_{p+1})$, apply (b) successively to the distinguished squares from step 4. This proves $P(W_1),\ldots,P(W_m)=P(U_p)$. If $V_p$ is empty, surjectivity gives $U_p=\emptyset$ and the affine base case already applies. Descending induction now proves $P(U_1)=P(T)$. The choice of $T$ was arbitrary, and $T=X$ is allowed via the identity map, proving every clause.

lean.statement: theorem qcqs_etale_distinguishedSquare_induction {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hXqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hXqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) (P : Over X → Prop) (h_iso : ∀ (T T' : Over X), IsChartwiseEtale T.hom → CompactSpace (Point T.left.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated T.left → IsChartwiseEtale T'.hom → CompactSpace (Point T'.left.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated T'.left → (T ≅ T') → (P T ↔ P T')) (h_affine : ∀ (T : Over X), IsChartwiseEtale T.hom → (∃ A : Over S, IsAffine A.left ∧ Nonempty (T.left.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj A)) → P T) (h_square : ∀ (W U V O : Over X), IsChartwiseEtale W.hom → CompactSpace (Point W.left.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated W.left → IsChartwiseEtale U.hom → CompactSpace (Point U.left.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated U.left → IsChartwiseEtale V.hom → CompactSpace (Point V.left.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated V.left → IsChartwiseEtale O.hom → CompactSpace (Point O.left.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated O.left → ∀ (i : U ⟶ W) (p : V ⟶ W) (a : O ⟶ U) (b : O ⟶ V), IsPullback a.left.hom b.left.hom i.left.hom p.left.hom → (∃ A : OpenSubspace W.left, ∃ e : U.left.obj.obj ≅ A.val.toFunctor, e.hom ≫ A.val.ι = i.left.hom.hom) → IsEtale p.left.hom.hom → (∃ A : Over S, IsAffine A.left ∧ Nonempty (V.left.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj A)) → ∀ C : ClosedSubspace W.left, IsReduced (C.val : AlgebraicSpace S) → pointImage C.val.arrow.hom.hom = (pointImage i.left.hom.hom)ᶜ → IsIso (Limits.pullback.snd p.left.hom C.val.arrow.hom) → P U → P V → P O → P W) : (∀ T : Over X, IsChartwiseEtale T.hom → CompactSpace (Point T.left.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated T.left → P T) ∧ P (Over.mk (𝟙 X))
